answer: Work waits on the karst until a stranger signs it off, and that signature becomes the jade of the next round. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. The design leans on bond keyed to a hardware root, reduced by each unverified claim, the cheapest attack must cost more than honest work. Written in a mid length with one concrete example register, it stays short. Reaching the sable of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys.
